newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares end firm, Telebras jumps.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares end firm, Telebras jumps.

text.p: Brazilian stocks continued higher on Wednesday, closing up 1.98 percent in another day of heavy volume, brokers said.
The Bovespa index of the 48 most active shares rose 258 points to 13,260 points at the close. Market turnover was 1.2 billion reais ($1.15 billion).
Benchmark Telebras again contributed to the market's rally, climbing 1.76 percent to 173.70 reais, but the highest rise was seen in the voting stock, which jumped 4.67 percent to 157 reais.
Traders said that investors moved to Telebras voting stock as the preferred share had risen too sharply in recent weeks.
Analysts said the decision by the U.S. Federal Reserve Open Market Committee (FOMC) to leave U.S. rates unchanged, although widely expected, also helped bolster market sentiment.
Although local investors have been the driving force behind the bolsa's recent surge, higher U.S. rates could encourage foreign funds to cut positions in the Brazilian stock market.
In addition to Telebras, all blue-chips posted further gains.

State oil firm Petrobras preferred rose 2.63 percent, closing at 312 reais, while federal power holding Eletrobras rose 0.3 percent to 665 reais.
Some banking stocks also performed well. Government bank Banco do Brasil rose 4.47 percent to 14.50 reais. The bank's stocks has been climbing recently on speculation over higher corporate earnings.

Itau preferred closed up 0.81 percent at 625 reais.
Another sector that outperformed the index was the steel industry.

Cosipa and Usiminas surged 9.84 percent and 5.69 percent, respectively, following a decision last month by a government antitrust agency to lift a ban that had prevented CSN from raising steel prices.
Although the decision only affected CSN, it is expected to be extended to Usiminas and Cosipa, which also have been forbidden to increase prices.
